#!/bin/sh
# THE CHANGED-FILE FMT CHECK — ONE definition, called by the gate's own fmt
# step (.github/workflows/checks.yml) and by `tools/work land`'s local
# preflight, so the two can never drift into two instruments.
#
#   sh tools/fmt_changed.sh <base> <head>     # the caller has refs (the gate)
#   sh tools/fmt_changed.sh --files <files…>  # the caller already diffed
#
# Every named `.av` file is run through `fmt --check`. The compiler is
# `${AVRA:-build/avra}` — the tree under test's OWN build. THE BRANCH'S
# COMPILER, NEVER A STALE STANDING ONE: a binary that predates the syntax a
# branch added REFUSES that branch's files and cannot report the canonical
# diff, so it would certify a file the gate then refuses. The gate has its
# own build; a lane's Sprite holds a branch build (`tools/work run`), and its
# synced tree carries no `.git`, which is why `--files` exists. Nothing
# here polls `main`: the refs are named, never watched.
set -eu
[ "$#" -ge 1 ] || { echo "fmt_changed: usage: sh tools/fmt_changed.sh <base> <head> | --files <files…>" >&2; exit 2; }
avra=${AVRA:-build/avra}
[ -x "$avra" ] || { echo "fmt_changed: no compiler at $avra" >&2; exit 2; }
```

```
// A `Bytes` const settles at compile time and lays out as the binary's
// own immortal box — the layout text shares. Each const is read back:
// a literal's octets, the empty value, octets that are not UTF-8, a
// list of them, a record field, a table computed by a fn, and one read
// by many calls (it must never be released).
type Framed = { mark: Bytes, n: int }

fn class_of(admit: fn(int) -> bool) -> Bytes { [if admit(i) { 1 } else { 0 } for i in 0..256].bytes() ?? "".bytes() }
fn digitish(c: int) -> bool { c >= 48 && c <= 57 }

const T: Bytes = "abc".bytes()
const E: Bytes = "".bytes()
const RAW: Bytes = [200, 0, 255, 7].bytes() ?? "".bytes()
const L: List<Bytes> = ["x".bytes(), "yz".bytes()]
const F: Framed = Framed { mark: "\r\n".bytes(), n: 2 }
const DIGITS: Bytes = class_of(digitish)

fn digits_in(s: string) -> int { s.bytes().run(0, DIGITS) }

fn many() -> int {
    mut total = 0
    for i in 0..1000 { total = total + T.length + DIGITS.length }
    total
}

"${T.text() ?? "?"} ${E.length} ${RAW.length} ${RAW.at(0)} ${RAW.at(1)} ${RAW.at(2)} ${L[1].text() ?? "?"} ${F.mark.length} ${F.n} ${digits_in("123x")} ${many()}"

    /// so pointer-riding registers cast down and bools widen in. A
    /// MATCH, never `is .I64`: this decides what crosses the extern

    fn rt_arg(callee: string, j: int, r: Reg) -> ptr {
        let v = self.vals[r.index]

        if j >= sig.params.length { return v }

//! `avra check <dir>` — a root's own SHAPE must speak. `build_workspace`'s
//! directory branch used to route every directory through `timed_workspace`

//! clean having examined nothing — silence the law forbids. `root_workspace`
//! is the fix: the same choice `file_workspace` already makes, for a

fn dir_named(name: string) -> string { "${check_nothing_base()}/${name}" }

/// A package root of one bare manifest, no `src/` — the shape this repo's
/// own root carries, and the shape that read clean before this fix.
fn rootless_root(name: string) -> string {
    let root = dir_named(name)
    let _ = make_dirs(root)
    let _ = write_text("${root}/avra.toml", "[package]\nname = \"${name}\"\nversion = \"0.0.1\"\n")
    root
}

/// A file directly in the root — the one shape `programs_workspace` reaches.
fn direct_program(root: string, name: string, text: string) {
    let _ = write_text("${root}/${name}.av", text)
}

/// Whether a source belongs to its module's listing: not excluded, and not a dependency's own

fn listed_in(manifest: PackageFacts, as_root: bool, path: string) -> bool {

    }

//! is settled in the instant it was sent, and a worker with nothing to
//! do asks its home for nothing more while it waits.
use @std.queue.{
    queue,
    worker,
    run,
    key,
    open_memory,
    Dead,
    Delivery,
    DrainError,
    Home,
    Order,

/// `under`, with each take counted.
fn counting(under: Home<int>, takes: Cell<int>) -> Home<int> {
    under with { take: (max: int) -> counted(takes, (under.take)(max)) }
}

fn counted<V>(n: Cell<int>, answer: V) -> V {
    n.set(n.get() + 1)
    answer
}

// proves: a named component instance writes type arguments after its
// word — `queue<Charge> charges { … }` pins the record's parameter
// from the WRITTEN type, so a queue whose head is a value-less name
// still seats its element type — and its name still lands as a child
// of a parent that lists it.
type Charge = { id: int }

component queue<T> {
    capacity: int = 1000
    dead: T? = null
}

// a parent whose list is of the same component routes the named
// instance to it, so the pre-scan sees past the written type args
component rack {
    qs: List<queue<Charge>> = []
}

queue<Charge> charges { capacity: 5 }
queue<int> counts { capacity: 2 }
rack board { charges }

"${charges.capacity} ${counts.capacity} ${board.qs.length}"
5 2 1
export enum ScheduleError { NoQueue, NoTick, TwoTicks, Line(why: CronError), Home(why: HomeError) }

/// A schedule's declaration. `name` heads the id of every tick it sends.
/// `at` is a cron line and `every` a span, each tick a whole number of
/// it past the epoch; exactly one is named. `catch_up` is how late a
/// tick may still be sent. `clock` is the wall it reads. `sent` fires
/// once a tick's item is in the queue, `missed` for the newest tick that
/// came due too long ago to send.
export component schedule<T> {
    name: string = ""
    at: Result<Cron, CronError>? = null
    every: Duration? = null
    sends: queue<T>?
    item: T
    catch_up: Duration = hours(1)
    clock: fn() -> Time = now

# A type-level annotation's NAMED argument is resolved as an expression

## Finding

On a TYPE, an annotation's positional arguments are read as the type's own fields, but a
named argument's value is resolved as an ordinary name. So `@tag(lane, absent: done_at)`
is `resolve.unresolved` ("`done_at` is not defined"). The annotation still runs, and

| type: `@tag(lane, done_at)` (positional) | passes; fields `lane,done_at` |
| field: `@tag(absent: done_at) lane` | passes; named reads `absent=done_at` |

commit b430bf349d87018953e4f61698cb91b0e37b8467
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   Thu Nov 19 01:16:21 2026 +0000

    program layer: an annotation names fields of the record it stands on, by seats of @std/meta's Field
    
    A seat of `@std/meta`'s `Field`, or a rest seat of a list of them, past a first seat taking the
    declaration's `Type`, takes the words written there as names of the annotated record's fields: a
    word is read among its fields, never as an expression, and crosses as that field's whole `Field`.
    A word naming no field is refused at the word with the field it's nearest offered; an argument

fn annotation_bodies(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, item: ReadItem) -> List<
    SignedBody,
> {

}

/// The annotation `a` on the statement `s`, as the bodies its callee and arguments are.
fn annotation_read(
    engine: QueryEngine,
    file: SourceFileAddress,
    item: ReadItem,
    s: StmtId,
    a: Annotation,
) -> List<SignedBody> {
    let seats = value_seats(engine, file, a.name)
    let written = [e for e in a.args if item.store.arg_label(e) == null]
    let words = seat_field_words(annotation_seats(engine, file, a.name), written)
    [annotation_body(item, s, a.callee, null, a.name)]
        .concat(
            [annotation_body(item, s, e, seat_filled(seats, written.index_of(e)), a.name) for e in a.args if !words.contains(e)],
        )
}

/// One expression of an annotation as a body: checked against `seat` where it fills one, else free.

/// Whether any of `seats` takes fields.
export fn seats_take_fields(seats: List<SignedParam>) -> bool { seats.any(!(field_take(it) is .Not)) }

/// The words among `args`, the unlabelled arguments an annotation writes, that fill a seat among
/// `seats` (past the first) taking fields.
export fn seat_field_words(seats: List<SignedParam>, args: List<ExprId>) -> List<ExprId> { flatten([words_filling(p, j, args) for j, p in seats]) }

fn words_filling(p: SignedParam, j: int, args: List<ExprId>) -> List<ExprId> {
    match field_take(p) {
        .Many -> args.drop(j),
        .One -> if j < args.length { [args[j]] } else { [] },
        .Not -> [],
    }

fn fields_named(
    engine: QueryEngine,
    file: SourceFileAddress,
    store: SyntaxArena,

) -> bool {

/// Each required context the program `file` starts reaches with nothing setting it, said where it
/// starts: the context, how it is reached, and the `dyn` call it crosses, where one does.
fn requireds_unset(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> List<Found> {
    let start? = first_running(engine, file, at) else { return [] }
    let declared = program_contexts(engine, file.package_name)
    if !declared.any(it.required) { return [] }
    let entry? = entry_lowered(engine, file) else { return [] }

    let store = read_item(engine, file, at).store

        at: store.stmt_span(start),
        args: [d.name, chain_said(r.chain), r.through?.subject ?? "", r.through?.held ?? ""],
    } for r in walked.reads for d in declared if d.key == r.key && d.required]
}

/// How a read is reached, as a reader follows it.
fn chain_said(chain: List<string>) -> string {
    if chain.is_empty() { return "where it starts" }
    ["`${n}`" for n in chain].join(" → ")
}

/// THE HOST INOUT LAW at the DECLARATION: a `mut` seat hands C the
/// ADDRESS of the caller's cell, so the cell's machine shape IS the
/// contract, and only a few shapes line up. A MANAGED value is out —
/// C cannot keep the refcount contract a box demands. A NARROW WIDTH
/// is out — the cell is 64 bits and a 32-bit write through it leaves
/// the top half stale, which is B3's defect wearing the other hat.
fn checked_extern(mut cx: TypeCx, s: StmtId, hname: string, hparams: List<Param>, hret: TypeRef) {
    for j, pp in hparams {
        if pp.promises.mutable && !inout_able(pp.ty) { seat_not_inout_able(cx, s, hname, j, pp) }
    }
    crossing_law(cx, s, hname, hparams)
    callback_law(cx, s, hname, hparams)
    let row? = rt_sigs().find(it.name == hname) else { return }
    row_shape_law(cx, s, row, hparams, hret)
    row_absence_law(cx, s, hname, hparams)
}

/// THE HOST FN LAW. An `extern fn` with a body DEFINES the symbol its
/// name spells: a host calls it by that name, and a bodiless `extern fn`
/// of the name elsewhere is answered by it. So its name is no runtime
/// row's — that symbol has a body already — and its seats and answer
/// are what crosses the seam in ONE register with no promise attached:

/// Where the trait `name` stands, as `@std/meta` hands a place: its file spelled by package and path
/// — never a path on disk — and its statement's span.
fn trait_place(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, item: ReadItem, name: string) -> Loc? {
    let s? = item.stmts.find((x: StmtId) -> item.store.trait_parts(x)?.name == name) else { return null }

}

/// A span of `file` as the place a meta value names: its file spelled by package and path.
fn meta_place(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, item: ReadItem, span: Span?) -> Loc? {
    let held? = span else { return null }
    let at = span_in_file(engine, file, item, held)
    Loc { file: spelled_file(file), lo: at.lo, hi: at.hi }
}

use @std.meta.{Type, Diagnostic, refuse_as_at, type_named, type_reached}

/// Says, for each field of `t`, what each field of its type names: read where that type was
/// declared, and read from `t`'s own file.
export fn reach(t: Type) -> List<Diagnostic> {
    [refuse_as_at("reach", t.at, [said(f.ty) for f in t.fields].join("; "), null)]
}

fn said(name: string) -> string {
    let held? = type_named(name) else { return "${name}: unseen" }
    "${name}: ${[reached(held, g.ty) for g in held.fields].join(", ")}"
}

fn reached(held: Type, name: string) -> string {
    "${name} reached ${type_reached(held, name)?.name ?? "unseen"}, named ${type_named(name)?.name ?? "unseen"}"
}
EOF

/// a path under it — is kept as the tree, and a path beside it (under `home`'s own directory)
/// as the tree's sibling, so a store read from another checkout of the same tree, or of a
/// package laid beside the same dependencies, names the same files. A longer name that only
/// begins like `home` is kept as it is; so is a path further out, and everything when `home`
/// is empty.
const TREE_MARK: string = "{tree}"

/// `text` with every whole `home` spelled as the tree: a path under it in one pass, then the
/// rare `home` that ends a path where it stands.
export fn saved_in(home: string, text: string) -> string {
    if home.is_empty() { return text }
    let beside = beside_of(home)
    if !text.contains(beside) { return text }
    let under = text.replace("${home}/", "${TREE_MARK}/").replace(beside, "${TREE_MARK}/../")
    if !under.contains(home) { return under }
    mut parts: List<string> = []
    mut rest = under
    mut at = rest.index_of(home)

        rest = after
        at = rest.index_of(home)
    }
    parts.push(rest)
    parts.join("")
}

/// neither, so no test writes the machine's cache or moves the tree its keys are spelled from.

    keys_spelled_from(tree)
    blobs_kept_in(machine)
    tree

/// A finding the item `at` of `file` holds, each place counted from the file's start: from its own
/// item's where it stands in another.
fn finding_in_file(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int, f: LawFinding) -> LawFinding {
    let home = f.item ?? at
    let placed = (p: FindingAt?) -> if p == null { null } else { file_placed(engine, file, home, p!) }
    f with { at: placed(f.at), named: placed(f.named), fixes: [fix_in_file(engine, file, home, x) for x in f.fixes], aside: aside_in_file(engine, file, at, f.aside), item: null }
}

/// An edit a finding the item `home` of `file` offers, counted from the file's start: one in another
/// item from that item's.
fn fix_in_file(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, home: int, x: FixAt) -> FixAt {
    let place? = x.at else { return x }
    x with { at: file_placed(engine, file, x.item ?? home, place), item: null }
}

/// An aside of a finding the item `at` of `file` holds, counted from the file's start: one in another
/// item from that item's.
fn aside_in_file(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int, aside: AsideAt?) -> AsideAt? {
    let a? = aside else { return null }
    let place? = a.at else { return a }
    a with { at: file_placed(engine, file, a.item ?? at, place), item: null }
}

//! The typing rule of a `const` in a body: its value checks against its annotation, and its name
//! binds to the annotation's type, or else to the value's. A named instance the entry builds where
//! it's written is the declaration, judged as one: its name binds to the declaration's type.
use core.{Checking, Seating, StmtChecks, StmtId}
use core.stmt.{ConstDecl}

impl StmtChecks for ConstDecl {
    fn stmt_checked(mut cx: Checking, s: StmtId) {
        let built = if cx.store.is_component_inst(s) { (cx.program.value_named)(self.name.of, null) } else { null }
        if built != null { return cx.bind(self.name.of, built!, true) }
        let declared = if self.ty == null { null } else { cx.written(self.ty!) }
        cx.const_opened(s)
        let read = cx.check_seated(self.value, declared, Seating.Binding(self.name.of))
        cx.const_closed()
        cx.bind(self.name.of, declared ?? read, true)
    }
}
        cx.bind_checked(s)
    }

    fn type_stmt(mut cx: TypeCx, s: StmtId) {
        check_const(cx, s)
    }

    fn lower_stmt(mut cx: LowerCx, s: StmtId) -> Reg? {
        if !cx.view.store.is_component_inst(s) { return null }
        let d? = cx.view.decls.decl_of(cx.view.file, s) else { return null }
        if !cx.view.decls.is_instance(d) { return null }
        cx.instance_value_reg(self.value, d)
    }
}

fn module_exports(engine: QueryEngine, package: string, local: List<string>, as_root: bool) -> ModuleExports {
    mut exports = module_own_exports(engine, package, local, as_root)
    for f in module_files(engine, package, local, as_root) {
        for u in [u for u in file_words(engine, f).uses if u.exported] { exports = exports.with_shapes(own_shapes(engine, f, u)) }
    }
    exports
}

impl ModuleExports {
    /// These exports with what `shapes` takes beside them, each under the name it's taken by.
    fn with_shapes(shapes: LineShapes) -> ModuleExports {
        mut components = self.components
        mut grammars = self.grammars
        mut instances = self.instances
        for c in shapes.components { components.set(c.word, (components.get(c.word) ?? []).concat([c])) }
        for g in shapes.grammars { grammars.set(g.word, (grammars.get(g.word) ?? []).concat([g])) }
        for i in shapes.instances { instances.set(i.name, (instances.get(i.name) ?? []).concat([i])) }
        self with { components: components, grammars: grammars, instances: instances }
    }
}

// A library that wants a declared grammar's parts — to print a usage line —
// has only `pattern()`, a string, so it re-reads the format by hand.
grammar Copy = "copy {src} to {dst...}:{mode: int}"

type HoleSeen = { name: string, ty: string, greedy: bool }

/// The holes, re-read from the pattern text: the format reader's rules,
/// copied — escapes (`{{`) and malformed holes are not handled.
fn holes_by_hand(pattern: string) -> List<HoleSeen> {
    mut out: List<HoleSeen> = []
    mut rest = pattern
    while rest.index_of("{") >= 0 {
        let open = rest.index_of("{")
        let shut = rest.index_of("}")
        let body = rest.substring(open + 1, shut)
        let colon = body.index_of(":")
        let written = if colon < 0 { body } else { body.substring(0, colon) }
        let ty = if colon < 0 { "string" } else { body.substring(colon + 1, body.length).trim() }
        let greedy = written.ends_with("...")
        let name = if greedy { written.substring(0, written.length - 3) } else { written }
        out.push(HoleSeen { name: name, ty: ty, greedy: greedy })
        rest = rest.substring(shut + 1, rest.length)
    }
    out
}

fn usage(pattern: string) -> string {
    [if h.greedy { "<${h.name}:${h.ty}...>" } else { "<${h.name}:${h.ty}>" } for h in holes_by_hand(pattern)].join(" ")
}

file_path: /work/avra-lane-parity-resolve-2-formats-design.md
--- content ---
# FORMATS — design note (B, then A, then C)

What exists today: `grammar R = "…"` is a record whose fields are its holes. On the layer its doors are
STATICS that item_formats.av generates as an `impl R { … }` from the record's `GrammarSpec { head, parts:
List<FormatPart { hole: Hole { name, ty: TypeRef?, greedy }, piece } }`. The four statics are `pattern`,
`parse`, `parse_octets` and `print`; the scan itself is the prelude's `format_spans`. On the old path the
same four are MethodRows (features/formats/mod.av). A pattern `"…"` in a `match` is `Pat.Format`,
read by the same reader (format.av `read_format`).

## B. `R.parts()` — a format's shape as a value

- **@std/meta declares the shape, once:** `FormatShape { head: string, holes: List<FormatHole> }` and
  `FormatHole { name: string, ty: string, greedy: bool, piece: string }`. `ty` is the type the hole
  binds, spelled as it is written: "string" where untyped.
- **The door is a fifth generated static,** `static fn parts() -> FormatShape`, beside `pattern()`.
  Its body is a record literal that item_formats writes from the same `GrammarSpec` it reads for
  `pattern()`. So it is read off the reader's parts, never re-parsed from the spelling, and no
  `crossing.av` row is needed: the value is static data the binary lays out like any const.
  `FORMAT_STATICS` gains "parts".
- **One definition:** the compiler converts `GrammarSpec → FormatShape` in exactly one verb,
  `format_shape(spec)`. B's door, C's library function and C's match law all read through it.
- **Old path:** the doors there are MethodRows. I'd give `parts` only to the layer and mark the gap
  (`tapes --new-only`), since the old path is being switched off. Say if you want the row as well.
- **Witness:** the README's wanted_door prints `3`, and `usage` drawn from `Copy.parts()` prints
  `<src:string> <dst:string...> <mode:int>`.

## A. A hole of any type that crosses as text

- **Today:** `reads_of(h)` matches `ty.name` against "string"/"int", the name-as-text dispatch
  CLAUDE.md forbids.
- **The decision moves to where the hole's type is RESOLVED.** Typing resolves the hole's `TypeRef`
  to a type and records a `HoleReading` fact per hole: `Text | Int | Form(ty)`.
  - `Text` and `Int` are told by the resolved type's identity (the owned `str`/`int`), not its spelling.
  - `Form(ty)` holds where `ty` implements `@std/text`'s `TextForm`. The trait is asked by DECLARED
    IDENTITY: on the layer the bound is the `SignedType` of the declaration `@std/text` exports
    (file + name), asked through `implements(engine, reader, ty, bound)` (item_methods.av, written
    impls first). On the old path it is the `DeclId` of that declaration through the impls table.
    No name is compared as text.
  - Anything else is refused once at the hole: "`T` crosses no text — implement `@std/text`'s
    `TextForm`" (type.format_parse, its voice re-worded to the law).
- **The readers take the fact, not the name:**
  - item_formats' `parse`: a `Form` hole is `T.from_text_form(span)?`, and absence fails the parse.
  - `print`: writes `r.f.text_form()`, and the round-trip guard (`survives`) runs on that same text.
  - A pattern arm (lower.av): binds through `T.from_text_form(span)`, and absence moves to the next arm.
  - `int` keeps its inline `format_int` path, and `string` its span.
- **One protocol a type:** parse and print both go through that type's `TextForm` impl; there is no
  registry and no second mechanism. `Time` works at once.
- **Witness:** the README's program prints `matched 7 miss 7 /items/i7`. A refusal case covers a hole
  typed by a type with no `TextForm`.

## C. `subsumes(A, B)` — "A accepts every text B accepts"

- **One definition, in @std/meta:** `export fn subsumes(a: FormatShape, b: FormatShape) -> Subsumed`,
  where `Subsumed { Covers, Misses, Unknown }`. It is pure Avra over B's value.
  - The compiler's match law calls it on `format_shape(spec)` of two arms.
  - `A.subsumes(B)` is a door that folds at compile time to `subsumes(A.parts(), B.parts()) ==
    .Covers`, so the compiler and every library ask the very same function.
- **Semantics, exactly the scan's:** a text matches F iff it begins with F's head and the scan
  succeeds. Hole k ends at its piece's FIRST occurrence (or its LAST where greedy), and a last piece
  "" means the hole takes the rest. Each span must also read as its type: `int` is `-?[0-9]+`,
  `string` is any text (empty included, as `format_spans` allows), and `Form(T)` is opaque.
- **The algorithm, where neither format holds a `Form` hole, is exact and decidable:**
  - Each such format denotes a REGULAR language.
    - A lazy hole followed by piece p is "a span holding no p, then p".
    - A greedy hole is "a span, then p, then a remainder holding no p".
    - Both are KMP automata over p.
  - The alphabet is partitioned into classes: each byte that occurs in either format's head or pieces,
    the digits, `-`, and "every other byte". The DFAs therefore stay small.
    - States per format are at most Σ|pieces| + |head| + (number of holes) × (KMP states of its piece).
  - "A covers B" is decided by emptiness of L(B) ∩ ¬L(A) on the product DFA, at most
    |DFA_A| × |DFA_B| states.
  - **The bound:** a cap of 4096 product states (the longest real route pattern gives well under 200).
    Past the cap it answers `Unknown`, and the walk itself is linear in the product.
- **A `Form(T)` hole is not regular.** Such a pair is decided only by STRUCTURAL ALIGNMENT:
  - Equal heads and equal pieces at each position.
  - Each of A's holes accepts at least what B's does at that position: `string` ⊇ everything,
    `int` ⊇ `int`, `Form(T)` ⊇ only `Form(T)`, the same type by identity.
  - Equal greed.
  - Alignment that holds is `Covers`; anything else is `Unknown`, never `Misses`. A `Form` hole can
    make no claim of missing.
- **Match reachability:**
  - In the layer's item_unreached, for each unguarded arm whose pattern is a format or a hole-free
    literal over a `string` subject, an earlier unguarded format arm `i` with
    `subsumes(i, j) == .Covers` warns `type.unreachable_arm` at arm j, naming arm i's pattern.
  - `Unknown` warns nothing.
  - A hole-free literal B needs no automaton: run A's scan on B's text, which is exact.
  - The README's three dead arms are each named. `{n: int}` over `{k: int}` is `Covers`: names don't
    matter, readings do.
- **std-http's `covers`/`shadows`** in route.av stay its own until it moves onto `subsumes`. Then there
  is no second copy; that is its owner's step, and I'd note it in the ROADMAP.
- **Old path:** it warns no format arm today. The new warnings are the layer's own (`tapes --new-only`
  doesn't apply to warnings), recorded as a known difference with its reason. Say if you'd rather the
  old path got the law too.

## Order and landing

- **B** comes first: it adds `FormatShape` and `format_shape`, which C's library function takes.
- **A** next: it adds `HoleReading`, and C reads the hole's reading through B's `ty`, plus the
  reading fact the match law needs.
- **C** last.
- Each is its own commit with its witnesses (prints cases, a refusal case for A, a warns case for C),
  and C's match law is witnessed in the README's three arms.
- **Questions for you:**
  1. The old-path doors for B and the old-path law for C, or layer-only?
  2. Is `@std/meta` the right home for `subsumes`, or a new `@std/formats`?

//! The formats semantics: dispatch only. The laws live in check.av,
//! the scan in lower.av. A feature matches its OWN variants and
//! delegates the rest — the seam routes every other pattern to its
//! owner before this is ever reached.
use core.{PatId, TypeId, Reg}
use features.{PatSemantics, TypeCx, LowerCx}
use features.formats.{format_types, format_accepts, format_binds}

export type FormatPatSemantics = {}

impl PatSemantics for FormatPatSemantics {
    fn pat_types(mut cx: TypeCx, p: PatId, expected: TypeId) -> List<TypeId> {
        // a feature cannot enumerate OTHER features' variants
        match cx.view.store.pat(p) {
            .Format(_, parts) -> format_types(cx, p, parts, expected),
            rest -> [],
        }
    }

    fn pat_accepts(mut cx: LowerCx, p: PatId, v: Reg, vty: TypeId) -> Reg {
        // a feature cannot enumerate OTHER features' variants
        match cx.view.store.pat(p) {
            .Format(head, parts) -> format_accepts(cx, p, head, parts, v, vty),
            rest -> reached_wrongly(cx),
        }
    }

    fn pat_binds(mut cx: LowerCx, p: PatId, v: Reg, vty: TypeId) -> List<Reg> {
        // a feature cannot enumerate OTHER features' variants
        match cx.view.store.pat(p) {
            .Format(_, parts) -> format_binds(cx, p, parts, v, vty),
            rest -> {
                cx.defect("a pattern that is no format reached the format binds")
                []
            },
        }
    }
}

/// The seam routes every pattern to its owner, so this cannot
/// arrive; refusing is the honest answer if the seam ever breaks.
fn reached_wrongly(mut cx: LowerCx) -> Reg {
    cx.defect("a pattern that is no format reached the format test")
    cx.const_bool(false)
}

//! A FORMAT PATTERN'S SCAN: one anchored left-to-right pass over the subject's octets — the head a
//! prefix, the last piece a suffix, and each piece between them found at its first place at or past
//! the cursor, or its last where its hole is greedy. Nothing goes back, so the scan is linear in the
//! subject, and a greedy hole may fail where its lazy twin would take: the place it took can leave a
//! later piece unfound. Each step runs only where every step before it held, which keeps a cursor
//! past the end from the search, whose start must stand inside. Each hole's span lands in cells the

//! reads its span once every span is found, still inside the verdict: a span that spells no `int`

    }

    /// Whether hole `k`'s span reads as a `ty` through `ty`'s own `from_text_form`, the value landing in
    /// its cell: octets only where they are text.
    mut fn form_read(v: Reg, bytes: bool, s: FormatScan, k: int, ty: SignedType) -> Reg {
        let callee? = (self.program.statics)(ty, FROM_TEXT_FORM) else {
            self.missed("`${ty.spelled()}.${FROM_TEXT_FORM}`, which a format hole of the type reads its span through")

        let held = self.call_row(self.laid_out(text), rt_sig_of("avra_str_of_bytes")!, [span])

    mut fn formed_into(callee: CalledFn, text: Reg, cell: Reg, ty: SignedType) -> Reg {

1://! A FORMAT PATTERN'S SCAN: one anchored left-to-right pass over the subject's octets — the head a
2://! prefix, the last piece a suffix, and each piece between them found at its first place at or past
3://! the cursor, or its last where its hole is greedy. Nothing goes back, so the scan is linear in the
4://! subject, and a greedy hole may fail where its lazy twin would take: the place it took can leave a
5://! later piece unfound. Each step runs only where every step before it held, which keeps a cursor
6://! past the end from the search, whose start must stand inside. Each hole's span lands in cells the
7://! steps write; a value is cut from them only where an arm binds it. A hole that reads as an `int`
8://! reads its span once every span is found, still inside the verdict: a span that spells no `int`
9://! fails the scan, as a missing piece does, and the `int` lands in the hole's own cell.

// ── The voices ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn not_text(mut cx: TypeCx, p: PatId, expected: TypeId) -> List<TypeId> {
    cx.emit(said_as("type.format", cx.pat_loc(p), format_on(cx.view.types.name_of(expected))))
    []
}

/// A format pattern matching a value of `found`, which is no text.
export fn format_on(found: string) -> Voice {
    Voice {
        message: "a format pattern reads text, found `${found}`",
        label: this_is(found),
        help: "a format matches a `string` or a `Bytes`",
    }
}

/// The two laws over the holes, each in its own words.
fn broken(mut cx: TypeCx, p: PatId, fault: Fault) -> List<TypeId> {
    match fault {
        .Adjacent(a, b) -> adjacent(cx, p, a, b),
        .Repeated(n) -> repeated(cx, p, n),
        .Unclosed(_) or .Stray(_) or .Malformed(_, _) -> [],
    }

'''/// Whether the hole `h`, its type written in `file` and signed by `signing`, reads its span as a type
/// that crosses text: none or `string`, an `int`, or a type that implements `@std/text`'s `TextForm`.
export fn read_as_text(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, signing: Signing, h: Hole) -> bool {
    let written? = h.ty else { return true }
    match hole_reading(signing.signed(written)) {
        .Text or .Int -> true,
        .Form(ty) -> crosses_text(engine, file, ty),
    }
}

/// Whether a value of `ty` crosses text: its type implements `@std/text`'s `TextForm`, the trait
/// asked by the declaration that package exports, never by its name.
export fn crosses_text(engine: QueryEngine, reader: SourceFileAddress, ty: SignedType) -> bool {
    let home? = dotted_file(engine, TEXT_MODULE) else { return false }
    let d? = resolved(engine, home, Space.Type, TEXT_FORM_TRAIT).named() else { return false }
    if d.kind != ItemKind.Trait { return false }
    let bound = Signing { engine: engine, file: d.file, type_params: [] }.signed(named_ref(d.name))
    implements(engine, reader.package_name, ty, bound) ?? false
}

/// The module that declares the trait a type crosses text through.
const TEXT_MODULE: List<string> = ["@std", "text"]

/// The trait a type crosses text through, as that module declares it.
const TEXT_FORM_TRAIT: string = "TextForm"

/// Every hole of a grammar the written item `at` of `file` declares that reads its span as a type
/// crossing no text, found at the declaration; handed the hole and the type.
fn grammar_holes_unread(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> List<Found> {
    let signing = Signing { engine: engine, file: file, type_params: [] }
    let item = read_item(engine, file, at)
    [Found { at: item.store.stmt_span(s), args: [p.hole.name, p.hole.ty!.name] } for s in item.stmts for spec in [item.store.grammar_of(s)] if spec != null for p in [q for q in spec!.parts if !read_as_text(engine, file, signing, q.hole)].take(1)]
}

/// a grammar's hole reads its span as a type that crosses text
export law grammar_hole_read_as_text {
    kind: "type.format_parse"
    reads: grammar_holes_unread
    voice: grammar_hole_words
    witness: "grammar Item = \\"/items/{n: float}\\"\\n"
}

fn grammar_hole_words(a: List<string>) -> Voice { hole_unread(a[0], a[1]) }

/// The `impl` a format gives its record, as a template of `file` at the record.'''),

fn template_nodes(store: SyntaxArena) -> List<ExprId> {
    flatten(
        [flatten([store.every_expr(x) for x in template_roots(store, ExprId { index: i })]) for i in 0..store.exprs.count()],
    )
}

/// The nodes the body `e` holds as a template written verbatim; none for any other node.
fn template_roots(store: SyntaxArena, e: ExprId) -> List<ExprId> {
    let body? = store.expr(e).body_of() else { return [] }
    match body.view {
        .Verbatim(stmts, arms) -> store
            .stmts_exprs(stmts)
            .concat([a.value for a in arms])
            .concat(flatten([some_list(a.guard) for a in arms])),
        .None or .Expanded(_) -> [],
    }
}

/// Whether the subject `subject` is a name nothing answers, among `unread`: a `match` over it chooses
/// nothing, and its arms are judged no further.
fn reads_unanswered(store: SyntaxArena, subject: ExprId, unread: List<FindingAt?>) -> bool {
    let at? = kept_at(store.expr_span(subject)) else { return false }
    unread.any(stands_at(it, at))
}

/// Whether the place `u`, where it is kept, is `at`.
fn stands_at(u: FindingAt?, at: FindingAt) -> bool {
    let held? = u else { return false }
    held.lo == at.lo && held.hi == at.hi
}

/// What one format answers of another: it accepts every text the other accepts, it misses one, or
/// that can't be told without reading a type's own text form.
export enum Subsumed {
    Covers
    Misses
    Unknown
}

/// WHETHER THE FORMAT `a` ACCEPTS EVERY TEXT `b` ACCEPTS, under the scan both are read by: the head a
/// prefix, the last piece a suffix, each piece between them at its first place (its last where its
/// hole is greedy), and each span read as its hole reads it. A `b` of no holes is one text, scanned by
/// `a`: exact. Otherwise `a` covers where its holes stand where `b`'s do — one head, one piece, one greed
/// at each place — each reading at least what `b`'s reads (text reads anything; an `int` an `int`;
/// a type that crosses text only itself), or where `a` is one hole reading text between a prefix of
/// `b`'s head and a suffix of `b`'s last piece. Anything else can't be told: the answer is `Unknown`,
/// never `Misses`.
export fn format_subsumes(a: FormatShape, b: FormatShape) -> Subsumed {
    if b.holes.is_empty() { return text_read_by(a, b.head) }
    if holes_aligned(a, b) || spans_around(a, b) { Subsumed.Covers } else { Subsumed.Unknown }
}

/// What the format `a` answers of the one text `text`: whether its scan takes it, and each span reads
/// as its hole reads; a span read through a type's text form can't be told here.
fn text_read_by(a: FormatShape, text: string) -> Subsumed {
    let spans? = format_spans(text.bytes(), a.head.bytes(), [h.piece.bytes() for h in a.holes], [h.greedy for h in a.holes]) else { return Subsumed.Misses }
    let reads = [span_read(h, text.substring(spans[2 * k], spans[2 * k + 1])) for k, h in a.holes]
    if reads.any(it == Subsumed.Misses) { return Subsumed.Misses }
    if reads.any(it == Subsumed.Unknown) { Subsumed.Unknown } else { Subsumed.Covers }
}

/// Whether the span `span` reads as the hole `h` reads it.
fn span_read(h: FormatHole, span: string) -> Subsumed {
    match h.reads {
        .Text -> Subsumed.Covers,
        .Int -> if format_int(span) != null { Subsumed.Covers } else { Subsumed.Misses },
        .Form -> Subsumed.Unknown,
    }
}

/// Whether `a`'s holes stand where `b`'s do, each reading at least what `b`'s reads: one head, and at
/// each place one piece and one greed, so every text `b` takes `a` splits alike.
fn holes_aligned(a: FormatShape, b: FormatShape) -> bool {
    a.head == b.head &&
        a.holes.length == b.holes.length &&
        (0..a.holes.length).all((k) -> hole_covers(a.holes[k], b.holes[k]))
}

/// Whether the hole `x` stands as `y` does and reads at least what `y` reads.
fn hole_covers(x: FormatHole, y: FormatHole) -> bool {
    x.piece == y.piece && x.greedy == y.greedy && reads_at_least(x, y)
}

/// Whether the hole `x` reads every span `y` reads: text reads anything, and any other reading only
/// its own type's.
fn reads_at_least(x: FormatHole, y: FormatHole) -> bool {
    match x.reads {
        .Text -> true,
        .Int -> y.reads == HoleRead.Int,
        .Form -> y.reads == HoleRead.Form && x.ty == y.ty,
    }
}

/// Whether `a` is one hole reading text between a prefix of `b`'s head and a suffix of `b`'s last
/// piece: every text `b` takes then starts and ends as `a` asks, its middle `a`'s span.
fn spans_around(a: FormatShape, b: FormatShape) -> bool {
    if a.holes.length != 1 || a.holes[0].reads != HoleRead.Text { return false }
    let last? = b.holes.last() else { return false }
    b.head.starts_with(a.head) && last.piece.ends_with(a.holes[0].piece)
}

fn package_text(files: Map<string, string>) -> string {
    joined(["// ${path}\n${text}" for path, text in files if !is_carried(path)], "\n")

/// Whether a package witness's file is the toolchain's, laid out beside the
/// program — never the witness itself, so a golden does not print it.
fn is_carried(path: string) -> bool { path.starts_with("/w/vendor/") || path.starts_with("/std/") }

/// A package witness compiled: its files laid out in memory at `/w`,
/// and what the program there says. One one-shot workspace is alive at a
/// time, so the one before is let go.
fn package_report(files: Map<string, string>) -> string {
    one_shot_let_go()
    let host = memory_host(files, files.keys())
    let ws = new_workspace(
        if files.keys().any(it.starts_with("/std/")) { host with { std_root: "/std" } } else { host },
        "/w",
        avra(),
    )
    ws.alone()
    let entry: string? = if files.has("/w/src/main.av") { "/w/src/main.av" } else { null }
    match ws.program(entry).check() { .Ok(warned) -> warned, .Err(report) -> report }
}

}

\`format_subsumes(a, b: FormatShape) -> Subsumed { Covers, Misses, Unknown }\` reads the scan's own rules:
- a \`b\` of no holes is one text, scanned by \`a\` (\`format_spans\`, each span read as its hole reads): exact;
- otherwise \`a\` covers where its holes stand where \`b\`'s do (one head, one piece and greed at each place), each reading at least what \`b\`'s reads (text anything, an \`int\` an \`int\`, a type crossing text only itself), or where \`a\` is one text hole between a prefix of \`b\`'s head and a suffix of \`b\`'s last piece;
- anything else is \`Unknown\`, never \`Misses\`, and warns nothing.
A hole's shape carries how it reads (\`HoleRead\`, from \`hole_reading\`'s identity), never its type's spelling. The law (\`arm_after_format\`, item_unreached.av) names the covering arm; the program layer's alone (differs.why). The witness harness's built programs carry the std prelude their \`@std/meta\` now reads (\`witness_host\`, one host for package and built witnesses). import re,glob,os,collections
defs={}

    if '/tests/' in f: continue
    for m in re.finditer(r'^export (?:fn|type|enum|const) (\w+)',open(f).read(),re.M):
        defs.setdefault(m.group(1),[]).append(f)
uses=collections.defaultdict(set)
for f in glob.glob('compiler/item_*.av'):
    s=open(f).read()
    for m in re.finditer(r'^use (features|compiler)(?:\.(\w+))?\.\{([^}]*)\}',s,re.M):
        for n in re.split(r'[,\s]+',m.group(3)):
            if not n: continue
            for d in defs.get(n,[]):
                if d.startswith('compiler/item_') or d.startswith('compiler/laws') : continue
                uses[d].add((n,os.path.basename(f)))
for d in sorted(uses):
    if 'resolve' in d or 'namespace' in d or 'voices' in d or 'modules' in d or 'walk' in d:
        print(d, sorted({n for n,_ in uses[d]}))

- The other callers keep the full resolution through a default parameter.
- The tradeoff: hand-written impls of generated types are found only where generated impls are consulted (the method lookup does so as a fallback), not where only the written ones are read.

### 2026-11-21T02:44:48 AGENT
I've found what causes the edit-signature +6.

`module_kept` is a plain query that doesn't cut, and it reads `module_bindings`, which moves on any signature edit because it carries each declaration's face. The engine checks a cut only right after an answer that moved. Past a query that doesn't cut, everything above it is re-run unchecked: here `file_scope`, and every law that reads it. The engine gap and the query were already in base57. My earlier commits are what made the `use`-line and impl laws read `file_scope` on every item, which is how the gap shows up.

The fix makes `module_kept` a cut query. A signature edit leaves its answer unchanged (no kept-apart name, no clash), so `file_scope` gets checked and stands.

A build with both changes in is running now: this cut and the impl-undeclared fix, still with the temporary trace. The replay will show whether edit-signature drops back from 57 toward base57's 51.

### 2026-11-21T03:04:39 AGENT
Making `module_kept`, `module_winners` and `module_declares` cut queries didn't change the count. edit-signature is still 57 and the same 8 `law_findings` re-run. These are temporary changes, not committed.

The reason is in the engine. When it checks whether a re-run answer still stands, it compares each read's whole answer, not the part the reader actually read. So the per-name split of those two parted queries buys nothing there. A law that reads one name's part re-runs whenever any name in the module moves, and a signature edit always moves the edited fn's part.

Fixing that comparison is engine work in std-program, outside my lane. The fix that's mine is to stop the `use`-line and impl laws from reading something that moves on every signature edit. To find which read that is, I've added one more temporary trace. It prints, for each `law_findings` answer that fails its check, the read that no longer holds. The build and replay are running.

    held

/// again by whoever is asking; absent where no held view holds them.
fn stated_elsewhere(engine: QueryEngine, view: ItemView) -> StatedHeld? {
    let other? = views_held()
        .get()
        .find_map(if it.holds(engine, view.file, view.at) { it.stated.get() } else { null }) else { return null }
    engine.reads_made_again(other.reads)
    other
}

/// Every item of `file` that runs a statement, read back into one store, each query it stands on
/// asked.
fn entry_read_back(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, placed: bool) -> EntryRead {
    let declaring = [d.item for d in file_declares(engine, file).names]
    let store = new_node_store()
    mut items: List<ItemBase> = []
    mut stmts: List<StmtId> = []
    for at in 0..item_count(engine, file) {
        if declaring.contains(at) && !runs_in(engine, file, at) && !builds_in(engine, file, at) { continue }
        let base = store.exprs.count()
        let running = read_into(
            engine,
            file,
            store,
            at,
            if placed { item_start(engine, file, at) } else { 0 },
        )
            .filter((s) -> runs(store, s))
        items.push(ItemBase { at: at, base: base, stmts: running })
        stmts = stmts.concat(running)
    }

### 2026-11-21T03:24:02 AGENT
I found what causes the edit-signature +6, and the fix is building now.

**Cause.** The law `assignment_lands` asks every item for its share of the file's entry, through `entry_share`. The early return covered only items that declare something and don't run. A `use` line or an `impl` declares nothing, so it went on to read the whole file's entry typing. That answer moves on any signature edit, so cache.av's five `use` items and its `impl` re-ran. They then found no share anyway, since a `use` or an `impl` runs no statement.

**Fix.** `entry_share` now returns early for any item that doesn't run. That covers `use` lines, impls and declarations alike. Findings don't change: an instance-building item already returned early under the old condition, and items that run are untouched.

**Working tree now holds only:**
- this fix, in item_assignments
- the impl-undeclared cycle fix, in item_methods and item_scope

The three cut-query changes (`module_kept`, `module_winners`, `module_declares`) and every temporary trace are reverted.
